benchmarks.task_description:
Live workers: no duplicate processes on restart

Fixes #6

## Cause
`stop-workers.sh` sent SIGTERM and returned immediately, so `run-workers.sh` started new processes while the old ones were still shutting down. A process that ignored SIGTERM kept running alongside the new one.

## Change
- `stop-workers.sh`: SIGTERM, wait up to `STOP_GRACE_SEC` (default 20 s) for every live worker to exit, then SIGKILL any left.
- `run-workers.sh`: `start` refuses to launch a service that is already running; the final status line reports `N copies` instead of ✓ when duplicates exist.
- Only processes matching `node .*apps/<service>/dist/main.js` are touched (the local dev stack runs `dist/main.js` without `apps/` and is unaffected).

## Tested
- Dummy service with 3 copies, one ignoring SIGTERM: all 3 stopped (1 forced after the grace period); the 7 real live workers were not touched.
- `bash -n` on both scripts.
benchmarks.solution_diff:
diff --git a/scripts/live/run-workers.sh b/scripts/live/run-workers.sh
index 6b35615..5c61191 100755
--- a/scripts/live/run-workers.sh
+++ b/scripts/live/run-workers.sh
@@ -20,7 +20,8 @@ LOGS="$ROOT/.local/live-logs"; mkdir -p "$LOGS"
 
 "$ROOT/scripts/live/stop-workers.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 cd "$ROOT"
-start() { # name entry
+start() { # name entry — refuses to start a second copy of a service
+  if pgrep -f "node .*apps/$1/dist/main.js" >/dev/null; then echo "  ✗ $1 is still running (pid $(pgrep -f "node .*apps/$1/dist/main.js" | tr '\n' ' ')) — not starting a second copy"; return; fi
   nohup node --enable-source-maps "apps/$1/dist/main.js" < /dev/null >> "$LOGS/$1.log" 2>&1 &
   echo "  started $1 (pid $!, log .local/live-logs/$1.log)"
 }
@@ -43,6 +44,9 @@ if [ -n "${BROWSER_DATABASE_URL:-}" ]; then
 fi
 sleep 5
 for s in $SERVICES; do
-  pgrep -f "apps/$s/dist/main.js" >/dev/null && echo "  ✓ $s running" || { echo "  ✗ $s stopped — last log lines:"; tail -5 "$LOGS/$s.log"; }
+  n=$(pgrep -f "node .*apps/$s/dist/main.js" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
+  if [ "$n" = 1 ]; then echo "  ✓ $s running"
+  elif [ "$n" = 0 ]; then echo "  ✗ $s stopped — last log lines:"; tail -5 "$LOGS/$s.log"
+  else echo "  ✗ $s has $n copies running — run scripts/live/stop-workers.sh, then start again"; fi
 done
 echo "Keep this Mac awake (e.g. caffeinate -s) — monitoring stops when it sleeps."
diff --git a/scripts/live/stop-workers.sh b/scripts/live/stop-workers.sh
index c2d482c..63a2327 100755
--- a/scripts/live/stop-workers.sh
+++ b/scripts/live/stop-workers.sh
@@ -1,7 +1,18 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 # Stop the live background services started by scripts/live/run-workers.sh (matched by their repo-relative entry point;
 # the local development stack runs `dist/main.js` from each app folder and is not affected).
-for s in scheduler worker-browser browser-runner worker-notify worker-deepscan worker-http egress-gateway; do
-  pkill -f "node .*apps/$s/dist/main.js" && echo "stopped $s"
+# Waits until every process has exited (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period) so a restart never overlaps the
+# old processes — overlapping copies of the scheduler or deep-scan worker process the same jobs twice.
+GRACE="${STOP_GRACE_SEC:-20}"
+SERVICES="scheduler worker-browser browser-runner worker-notify worker-deepscan worker-http egress-gateway"
+for s in $SERVICES; do
+  pkill -TERM -f "node .*apps/$s/dist/main.js" && echo "stopping $s"
+done
+for _ in $(seq "$GRACE"); do
+  pgrep -f "node .*apps/(${SERVICES// /|})/dist/main.js" >/dev/null || break
+  sleep 1
+done
+for s in $SERVICES; do
+  pkill -KILL -f "node .*apps/$s/dist/main.js" && echo "forced $s (did not exit within ${GRACE}s)"
 done
 exit 0

benchmarks.task_description:
CI: allowlist Pencil design canvases in the secret scan

Fixes #10

## Change
`.gitleaks.toml`: add one path to the allowlist — `^design/[^/]+\.pen$` (Pencil design canvases only).

## Why
`design/sitesentinel.pen` triggers the generic high-entropy `generic-api-key` rule. It is an encoded design file containing only placeholder UI text. The owner chose this option (scoped allowlist) over rewriting pushed history.

## Scope kept narrow
- Only `.pen` files directly in `design/`. The exported PNGs, all code, config, scripts and docs remain scanned.
- Existing allowlist entries unchanged.

## Tested (gitleaks 8.24.3, same as CI)
- Current tree: no leaks.
- Commit range `origin/main..HEAD` (includes d0823c1): no leaks.
- Canary: a fake `sk_live_…` key added under `apps/` is still detected (1 leak).

benchmarks.task_description: fix(docs): let Tab move focus out of the live code editors # Pull Request ## Description Every live example on bestax.io trapped keyboard focus. react-live's editor defaults to `tabMode="indentation"`, so Tab and Shift+Tab indented and outdented the code instead of moving focus, and a keyboard user who tabbed into an example couldn't leave it (WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, Level A). This passes `tabMode="focus"` to the one `LiveEditor` every live fence renders through, in `docs/src/theme/CodeBlock/index.js`, which hands both keys back to the browser. - [ ] bulma-ui (`@allxsmith/bestax-bulma`) - [ ] create-bestax (`create-bestax`) - [x] docs (`@allxsmith/bestax-docs`) - [x] Other (please specify): a root `scripts/` test What readers give up inside an example: Tab and Shift+Tab no longer indent or outdent, and Backspace in leading spaces deletes one space instead of two. Typing spaces still indents. The indentation mode also set a tab size of 2 on the editor, so the editor's style now sets `tabSize: 2` to keep any pasted tab the same width. `scripts/docs-live-editor.test.mjs` parses `docs/src` and finds each JSX element rendering react-live's `LiveEditor` or `Editor`, imported from `react-live` by name, alias or namespace. Each must carry the literal `tabMode="focus"` with no spread after it that could replace it. With the attribute removed, it fails and names `docs/src/theme/CodeBlock/index.js`. ## Related Issue(s) Fixes #2177 Refs #2180 (the editor's missing focus ring and accessible name, which this doesn't change) ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Performance - [ ] Build tooling - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Checklist - [x] My code follows the project style guidelines - [x] I have performed a self-review of my code - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [ ] I have added/updated documentation as needed - [ ] I have updated Storybook stories as needed (bulma-ui) - [ ] My changes require a change to the documentation - [x] All new and existing tests passed - [ ] Any relevant dependencies are updated - [ ] If this PR changes commands, conventions, or package structure, the affected `CLAUDE.md` files are updated ## Screenshots / Demos | Before (bestax.io): three Tabs indent the line and focus stays in the editor | After (this branch): one Tab moves focus to the next heading link; the code is unchanged | | --- | --- | | | | ## Additional Context Checked in Chrome with real key presses on the Button page's first example. Before (bestax.io): three Tabs indented the line by six spaces, four Shift+Tabs took it back out, and focus stayed in the editor throughout. After (this branch): Tab moves focus to the next heading's anchor link, Shift+Tab to the example's copy button, and the code is unchanged. Local review findings left as they are: - **An Escape-to-release mode instead of `tabMode="focus"`.** It would keep Tab-to-indent, but it needs a key handler and a visible hint to meet 2.1.2, which is more to get right than a docs example's indenting is worth. #2177 picked `tabMode="focus"`. - **Backspace at the start of a line in browsers without `contentEditable="plaintext-only"`.** With no indent width, use-editable's own Backspace handler deletes nothing at column 0, so a line can't be joined to the one above. Only browsers that lack plaintext-only take that path (Firefox added it in 136), and react-live's focus mode can't avoid it. - **Editors the test can't see:** one rendered with `React.createElement`, through a variable, from a re-exporting module, or in an MDX page. Live fences all render through the CodeBlock theme, and the test's header says which imports it reads. - **No visible focus ring, and no role or name, on the editor.** They predate this change, since the editor was always a Tab stop. Filed as #2180, since the ring's look needs Alex's eye. - **Moving the recursive file walker into `scripts/lib` to share with two sibling tests, and loading TypeScript through `createRequire`.** Both are refactors of other tests, outside this fix. `scripts/client-directive.test.mjs` already imports TypeScript the same way.

Refresh Final - gh pr checkout 4

Agente MOSSAD UM
Leonardo Haim Nigri

benchmarks.task_description:
[FIX] GROMO-2905 iOS 운영 빌드 Fastfile 의 Sentry 확인 스크립트 경로를 고친다

## Jira
- [GROMO-2905](https://romance.atlassian.net/browse/GROMO-2905)

## 변경 유형
FIX

## Summary
iOS 2.3.8 운영 빌드(`./testflight.sh` → `fastlane beta`)가 `archive_and_upload` 첫 줄의 `sentry-xcode.sh check-release` 에서 `app/scripts/sentry-xcode.sh: No such file or directory`(종료 127)로 멈췄다. 티켓 2895(#1671)에서 넣은 경로가 lane 실행 중 `__dir__` 기준으로 한 단계 위(`app/`)를 가리켰다.

## 커밋 목록
- ce504471a [FIX] GROMO-2905 iOS 운영 빌드 Fastfile 의 Sentry 확인 스크립트 경로를 고친다

## Changes
- `app/app-dev/ios/fastlane/Fastfile` `archive_and_upload`: `sentry_script` 를 맨 위에서 고정한 `IOS_DIR` 기준 `../scripts/sentry-xcode.sh`(= `app/app-dev/scripts/sentry-xcode.sh`)로 바꾼다. 같은 파일의 `HERMES_CLI_PATH`·`APP_VERSION_SCRIPT` 도 `IOS_DIR` 기준이다

## 빌드/배포 영향
- [x] JS만 변경 → OTA 가능(네이티브 빌드 불필요) — 앱 코드 변경 없음. iOS 운영 빌드 스크립트만 고친다

## 주의사항
- 로컬 확인: 같은 워크트리에서 `bash app/app-dev/scripts/sentry-xcode.sh check-release` 는 종료 0(인증 성공), `ruby -c` 통과. 실제 업로드는 머지 뒤 2.3.8 운영 빌드로 확인한다.
- Android AAB(2.3.28)는 이미 만들어 Play 내부 테스트에 올렸으므로 이 머지로 새 Android 자동 빌드를 돌리지 않는다. [skip ci]

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(infra): reinicia o Kong quando o deploy recria market-data ou web

## Problema
O deploy da v0.2.1 reprovou no smoke e fez rollback para a v0.2.0: `/v1/openapi.json` voltou 404. Nos logs do job, as requisições chegaram ao **market-data-worker**: ao recriar o `market-data`, o Kong continuou usando o IP cacheado do container antigo, e o Docker reaproveitou esse IP no worker (que só serve `/v1/health`). Por isso o health passou e o OpenAPI não.

## Correção
`depends_on` do Kong em `compose.prod.yml` com `restart: true` para `market-data` e `web` (os dois upstreams do Kong): sempre que o compose recria um deles, reinicia o Kong, que resolve o nome de novo.

## Como validei
- `docker compose config` do prod renderiza `restart: true` nas duas dependências.
- `make lint test`: verde.
- A troca de IP é aleatória, então não dá para forçar localmente; o smoke com rollback automático continua como rede de segurança. Confiro no deploy da 0.2.2.

Closes #81

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

index 35544f1..476e738 100644
--- a/infra/docker/compose.prod.yml
+++ b/infra/docker/compose.prod.yml
@@ -262,9 +262,12 @@ services:
       - ./infra/kong:/kong:ro
     ports:
       - "127.0.0.1:8000:8000"
+    # restart: o Kong guarda o IP resolvido do upstream. Quando o deploy recria
+    # market-data ou web, o IP antigo pode ir para outro container (ja foi para o
+    # market-data-worker, que so serve health); reiniciar o Kong resolve de novo.
     depends_on:
-      market-data: { condition: service_healthy }
-      web: { condition: service_healthy }
+      market-data: { condition: service_healthy, restart: true }
+      web: { condition: service_healthy, restart: true }
     healthcheck:
       test: ["CMD", "kong", "health"]
       interval: 10s
